newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Colonial powers should help rebuild Congo - Kabila.
newsitem.headline: Colonial powers should help rebuild Congo - Kabila.

text.p: Democratic Republic of the Congo leader Laurent Kabila told developed nations on Monday that colonialism made them wealthy, and asked them to help pay for reconstructing the shattered former Zaire.
"We remind the wealthy northern nations that their riches and well-being come largely from their colonial heritage," he said to applause at an Independence Day rally.
"We invite all signatories of the Berlin Treaty to bring their contribution to African rebirth and reconstruction. We also address ourselves to the United States, Canada and Japan."
Europe's colonial powers met in Berlin in 1885 and agreed the division of Africa.
In his first major public speech since his inauguration as president in May, Kabila also asked the World Bank and U.N. agencies to assist in restoring prosperity and order to the country.
He addressed thousands of supporters at the rally in Kinshasa's Stadium of Martyrs, after a victory march by his rebel forces who in May ended president Mobutu Sese Seko's corrupt 32-year rule.
Belgian granted independence in 1960 to its Congo, founded and exploited as a private fiefdom by King Leopold.
Mobutu, who ruled Africa's third-largest country single-handedly from 1965 to until mid-May, long played down Independence Day.
"This anniversary marks a renaissance for our country," said Kabila, who a year ago was unknown to most of Congo's citizens.
On Monday, some women marched through the stadium in colourful dresses bearing his portrait.
Opposition leaders, angered at Kabila's ban on political activity, called for street marches on Monday's holiday, but the city was quiet.
State television had warned that protesters would be dealt with harshly. The city had a morning of unrest last week after the brief detention of opposition politician Etienne Tshisekedi.
Heads of states of several African countries including Rwanda and Burundi, close allies in Kabila's seven-month war overthrowing Mobutu, attended the celebrations.
